questions.q: Which part of Indian Constitution deals with the election of the Vice President?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Part V.

Key Points

• Part V of the Indian Constitution is titled "The Union".

• It encompasses provisions related to the President, the Vice-President, the Council of Ministers, and the Parliament.

• Articles 52 to 151 deal with the executive, legislative, and administrative functions of the Union Government.

• The election of the Vice President of India is specifically covered under Articles 63 to 71 in Part V of the Constitution.

Additional Information

• Part IV

• Part IV of the Indian Constitution is titled "Directive Principles of State Policy".

• It contains Articles 36 to 51.

• These articles guide the State in making laws and policies to establish a just society in the country.

• However, they are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by any court.

• Part III

• Part III of the Indian Constitution is titled "Fundamental Rights".

• It contains Articles 12 to 35.

• These articles guarantee essential rights such as equality, freedom, and protection against exploitation.

• These rights are justiciable, meaning they can be enforced by the courts.

• Part VI

• Part VI of the Indian Constitution is titled "The States".

• It contains Articles 152 to 237.

• This part deals with the executive, legislative, and administrative structure of the States.

• It outlines the roles and responsibilities of the Governor, State Legislature, and Council of Ministers.

questions.q: In which of the following games is the 'Baulk Line' used?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kabaddi.

Key Points

• The 'Baulk Line' is a critical feature in the game of Kabaddi.

• It is used to determine the playing area for raiders and defenders.

• A raider must cross the baulk line to make their raid valid.

• Crossing the baulk line puts pressure on the defenders and adds a strategic element to the game.

Additional Information

• Kabaddi

• Kabaddi is a contact team sport that originated in India.

• The objective of the game is for a single player, known as a "raider," to run into the opposing team's half of the court, tag out as many of their defenders as possible, and return to their own half of the court, all without being tackled by the defenders, and in a single breath.

• The baulk line plays a critical role during a raid. A raider must cross this line to make their raid valid, and it acts as a challenge for both raiders and defenders.

• Kabaddi has gained international recognition and is played in several countries, with professional leagues and tournaments being organized globally.

• Badminton

• Badminton is a racquet sport played using racquets to hit a shuttlecock across a net.

• It is usually played as a singles or doubles game.

• The boundaries of the playing area in badminton are defined by lines on the court, but terms like "baulk line" are not used in this sport.

• Tennis

• Tennis is a racquet sport that can be played individually against a single opponent (singles) or between two teams of two players each (doubles).

• The court is rectangular and bounded by lines, but does not include a "baulk line."

• Players use the tennis racquet to hit the ball over a net into the opponent's court.

• Kho-Kho

• Kho-Kho is a traditional Indian sport that involves two teams of twelve players each.

• The game is played on a rectangular field, and the main objective is to avoid being tagged by members of the opposing team.

• While the sport involves various lines and zones, such as the central line and the posts, the term "baulk line" is not applicable to Kho-Kho.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: Light year is the unit of distance.
Light year is the distance travelled by light in one year.
Light year is the unit of time.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Light year is the unit of time..

Key Points

• A light year is not a unit of time; it is a unit of distance.

• A light year is the distance that light travels in one year in a vacuum.

• The concept of a light year is used in astronomy to measure vast distances between celestial objects.

• One light year is approximately 9.461 trillion kilometers (5.879 trillion miles).

Additional Information

• Light Year:

• A light year is defined as the distance that light travels in a vacuum in one Julian year (365.25 days).

• This distance is used in astronomy to express the scale of the universe.

• It allows astronomers to measure distances between stars, galaxies, and other celestial objects.

• Angstrom:

• An angstrom is a unit of length used primarily in the field of physics and chemistry.

• It is equal to 10⁻¹⁰ meters or 0.1 nanometers.

• Angstroms are often used to measure wavelengths of light, atomic radii, and the size of molecules.

• Distance Measurement in Astronomy:

• Astronomers use various units to measure distances, including astronomical units (AU), light years, and parsecs.

• 1 AU is the average distance from the Earth to the Sun, approximately 149.6 million kilometers.

• 1 parsec is equal to about 3.26 light years or 31 trillion kilometers.

• These measurements help in understanding the vastness of space and the relative positions of celestial bodies.

questions.q: What is the economic justification for subsidies in the agriculture sector?
options: It is mostly used to provide benefits for rich farmers.
It is a part of government expenditure in the service sector.
It is an incentive to provide the benefits of advanced technology and decrease the cost of production.
It is used to provide benefits for capital goods producers in agriculture.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is It is an incentive to provide the benefits of advanced technology and decrease the cost of production.

Key Points

• Subsidies in the agriculture sector are primarily aimed at reducing the cost of production for farmers.

• They help in making advanced technologies and farming techniques more accessible to farmers, which can lead to increased productivity.

• By lowering production costs, subsidies can help in stabilizing food prices and ensuring food security.

• Such incentives also encourage farmers to adopt sustainable agricultural practices, which can lead to long-term benefits for the environment and the economy.

Additional Information

• Subsidies

• Subsidies are financial aids provided by the government to support economic sectors, making goods and services more affordable.

• They can be in the form of direct cash transfers, tax breaks, or reduced prices.

• Agricultural Subsidies

• Agricultural subsidies are designed to support farmers by reducing the cost of inputs such as seeds, fertilizers, and machinery.

• These subsidies aim to enhance agricultural productivity and ensure food security.

• Food Security

• Food security means ensuring that all people have access to sufficient, safe, and nutritious food to maintain a healthy and active life.

• It is dependent on food availability, accessibility, and proper utilization.

• Sustainable Agriculture

• Sustainable agriculture involves farming practices that are environmentally friendly, economically viable, and socially responsible.

• It aims to meet the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.

questions.q: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 empowers the  to establish authorities charged with the mandate of preventing environmental pollution in all its forms.
questions.solution:

Key Points

• The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, is an Act of the Parliament of India, enacted in the wake of the Bhopal Gas Tragedy.

• The Act empowers the Central Government to make rules to regulate environmental pollution and to establish authorities for the purpose.

• It provides the Central Government with the authority to take all necessary measures to protect and improve the quality of the environment.

• It encompasses a wide range of regulations and standards to control pollution and manage hazardous substances.

Additional Information

• Environment (Protection) Act, 1986

• The Act was passed in response to the need for overarching legislation to protect and improve the environment.

• The Act gives the Central Government the power to take measures for environmental protection, such as setting standards for emissions or discharge of environmental pollutants from various sources.

• It provides a framework for coordinating the activities of various central and state authorities established under other laws to ensure environmental protection.

• The Act also includes provisions for penalties for contravention of the standards and restrictions set by the government.

• Key Provisions of the Act

• Section 3: Empowers the Central Government to take measures to protect and improve the environment and to prevent, control, and abate environmental pollution.

• Section 6: Empowers the Central Government to make rules to regulate environmental pollution, including standards for the quality of the environment, and the maximum allowable concentrations of various pollutants.

• Section 15: Provides for penalties for non-compliance with the provisions of the Act, including imprisonment and fines.

• Section 19: Allows any person to file a complaint in a court of law against anyone who fails to comply with the Act's provisions.

• Importance of the Act

• The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, serves as a comprehensive framework for the protection and improvement of the environment in India.

• It addresses the need for a unified approach to environmental regulation and management.

• The Act empowers the government to take proactive measures to prevent environmental degradation and to respond effectively to environmental emergencies.

• It plays a crucial role in ensuring sustainable development and safeguarding public health and well-being.

questions.q: Which of the following Articles and Parts of the Indian Constitution deal with the State Legislature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Articles 168 to 212 in Part VI.

Key Points

• Articles 168 to 212 in Part VI of the Indian Constitution deal with the State Legislature.

• The State Legislature consists of the Governor and one or two Houses, as the case may be.

• In some states, the legislature is bicameral, consisting of the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council, while in others, it is unicameral, consisting only of the Legislative Assembly.

• These articles lay down the composition, duration, and functions of the State Legislatures.

Additional Information

• Article 168: This article specifies the composition of the State Legislature, which can be either unicameral (with only the Legislative Assembly) or bicameral (with both the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council).

• Article 170: This article deals with the composition of the Legislative Assemblies, including the number of seats and the delimitation of constituencies.

• Article 171: This article outlines the composition of the Legislative Councils, including the method of election and nomination of members.

• Article 174: This article mandates that the Governor shall summon the Legislature at least once every six months.

• Article 176: This article requires the Governor to address the Legislature at the commencement of the first session after each general election and at the commencement of the first session of each year.

• Article 178: This article provides for the election of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly.

• Article 194: This article grants certain privileges and immunities to the members of the State Legislature.

• Article 212: This article states that the validity of any proceedings in the Legislature of a state shall not be called in question on the ground of any alleged irregularity of procedure.

questions.q: The upper portion of the Earth is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lithosphere.

Key Points

• The Lithosphere is the rigid, outermost shell of the Earth, encompassing both the crust and the uppermost part of the mantle.

• It is divided into tectonic plates that float on the semi-fluid asthenosphere beneath it.

• The thickness of the Lithosphere varies, being thinnest at mid-ocean ridges and thickest beneath continental crust.

• The Lithosphere is crucial for plate tectonics, as its movements and interactions cause earthquakes, volcanic activity, and the creation of mountain ranges.

Additional Information

• Stratosphere

• The Stratosphere is the second major layer of Earth's atmosphere, lying above the Troposphere and below the Mesosphere.

• It extends from about 10 km to 50 km above Earth's surface.

• This layer contains the ozone layer, which absorbs and scatters ultraviolet solar radiation.

• Commercial jet aircraft typically fly in the lower stratosphere.

• Troposphere

• The Troposphere is the lowest layer of Earth's atmosphere, extending from Earth's surface up to about 8-15 km.

• It contains approximately 75% of the atmosphere's mass and 99% of its water vapor and aerosols.

• Weather events occur in the Troposphere.

• Mesosphere

• The Mesosphere is the layer of the atmosphere above the Stratosphere and below the Thermosphere.

• It extends from about 50 km to 85 km above the Earth's surface.

• This layer is where most meteorites burn up upon entering the Earth's atmosphere.

• The temperature decreases with altitude in the Mesosphere.

questions.q: In West Bengal, how many rice crops are grown in a year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Three.

Key Points

• In West Bengal, rice is a major crop and is cultivated three times a year.

• The three main rice crops are known as Aus, Aman, and Boro.

• Aus rice is sown during the pre-monsoon season (March-April) and harvested in the summer (June-July).

• Aman rice is sown during the monsoon season (June-July) and harvested in the winter (November-December).

• Boro rice is sown during the winter season (December-January) and harvested in the summer (April-May).

Additional Information

• Aus Rice:

• Also known as autumn rice, it is one of the early varieties of rice cultivated in the pre-monsoon period.

• It is typically sown in March-April and harvested by June-July.

• This variety of rice requires less water compared to the other two, making it suitable for areas with less rainfall.

• Aman Rice:

• Also known as winter rice, it is a monsoon-season crop.

• It is sown in June-July and harvested by November-December.

• This variety of rice depends heavily on the monsoon rains for its cultivation.

• Boro Rice:

• Also known as summer rice, it is cultivated in the winter season.

• It is sown in December-January and harvested by April-May.

• This variety requires irrigation facilities as it is grown during the dry season.

questions.q: Which of the following sectors in India faces seasonal unemployment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Agriculture.

Key Points

• Agriculture is a sector that is highly dependent on seasons and climatic conditions, leading to seasonal unemployment.

• During the off-season, agricultural workers may not find work, leading to temporary unemployment.

• This type of unemployment typically affects rural areas where agriculture is the primary occupation.

• Seasonal unemployment in agriculture can be mitigated by providing alternate employment opportunities during the off-season.

Additional Information

• Seasonal Unemployment:

• Seasonal unemployment occurs when people are unemployed at certain times of the year because their work is seasonal in nature.

• Common sectors that face seasonal unemployment include agriculture, tourism, and construction.

• In agriculture, this type of unemployment happens between planting and harvesting seasons.

• To mitigate seasonal unemployment, workers often seek alternative employment during the off-season or may participate in government employment schemes.

• Cyclical Unemployment:

• Cyclical unemployment occurs due to the fluctuations in the business cycle—during recessions, demand for goods and services decreases, leading to job losses.

• This type of unemployment is typically temporary and can be addressed through economic policies that stimulate demand.

• Structural Unemployment:

• Structural unemployment is caused by mismatches between the skills of the unemployed and the skills needed for available jobs.

• This can be due to technological changes, shifts in the economy, or other long-term changes.

• Re-training and education programs can help reduce structural unemployment.

• Frictional Unemployment:

• Frictional unemployment occurs when people are temporarily unemployed while transitioning from one job to another.

• This is a natural form of unemployment and is often short-term.

• It is also considered a sign of a healthy economy as workers move to jobs that better match their skills and preferences.

questions.q: The revolution of 1857 started in May from which of the following cantonments in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Meerut.

Key Points

• The revolution of 1857, also known as the First War of Indian Independence, started from the cantonment of Meerut.

• The revolt began on May 10, 1857, when Indian soldiers in Meerut rebelled against the British officers.

• The immediate cause of the revolt was the introduction of new rifle cartridges rumored to be greased with cow and pig fat, offending both Hindu and Muslim soldiers.

• Meerut was one of the largest military cantonments in India at the time, making it a significant starting point for the uprising.

Additional Information

• Causes of the Revolt

• Political Causes: The annexation policies of the British, such as the Doctrine of Lapse, created widespread resentment among Indian rulers.

• Economic Causes: The heavy taxation and exploitation of Indian farmers, artisans, and the destruction of traditional industries led to economic distress.

• Social and Religious Causes: The British social reforms, which were seen as interference in traditional customs and religious practices, angered many Indians.

• Spread of the Revolt

• After Meerut, the revolt quickly spread to other parts of India, including Delhi, Kanpur, Lucknow, Jhansi, and Gwalior.

• Many Indian rulers and soldiers joined the rebellion, seeing it as an opportunity to regain their lost power and territories.

• Suppression of the Revolt

• The British used superior military force and strategic alliances with some Indian rulers to suppress the revolt.

• By 1858, the British had regained control over most of the rebellious areas, marking the end of the revolt.

• Consequences of the Revolt

• The revolt led to the end of the East India Company's rule in India, and the British Crown took direct control of the Indian administration.

• The British government made several administrative and military reforms to prevent any future rebellions.

• The revolt also marked the beginning of a stronger nationalistic movement in India, leading to the eventual struggle for independence.

questions.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of both mammals and birds?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Warm blooded.

Key Points

• Mammals and birds are both warm-blooded, meaning they can regulate their body temperature internally.

• This characteristic allows them to maintain a stable body temperature regardless of the external environment.

• Being warm-blooded helps these animals to remain active in a wide range of temperatures.

• Warm-blooded animals have higher metabolic rates compared to cold-blooded animals, which helps in supporting their active lifestyles.

Additional Information

• Viviparity

• Viviparity is the mode of reproduction in which the embryo develops inside the body and is born live.

• Synapsis is the pairing of homologous chromosomes during prophase I of meiosis.

For triangles, which of the following statement(s) are true?

(a) Sum of interior angles is 180°.

(b) All interior angles can’t be equal.

(c) Can have at the most one obtuse angle.

(d) Sum of two sides may or may not be equal to the third side.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Evaluate each statement logically based on the geometric properties of a planar triangle.

(a) The sum of interior angles is exactly 180°, which is a universally fundamental property. (True)

(b) An equilateral triangle has three equal interior angles of 60° each. (False)

(c) A triangle can have at most one obtuse angle (>90°), else the sum exceeds 180°. (True)

(d) The triangle inequality theorem states the sum of two sides must be strictly greater than the third side. (False)

∴ The correct answer is (a) and (c).

Analysis:

⇒ Statement (a): By the Angle Sum Property of a triangle, the sum of all three interior angles is always equal to 180°. Hence, statement (a) is logically sound.

⇒ Statement (b): All interior angles of a triangle can indeed be identical. For example, in an equilateral triangle, all three angles measure exactly 60°. Hence, statement (b) is invalid.

⇒ Statement (c): If a triangle possessed two obtuse angles (both greater than 90°), their combined sum would be strictly greater than 180°, defying the core angle sum property. Thus, a triangle can possess at most one obtuse angle. Hence, statement (c) is logically sound.

⇒ Statement (d): The Triangle Inequality Theorem dictates that the sum of the lengths of any two sides of a triangle must always be strictly greater than the length of the third side. It can never be equal or less. Hence, statement (d) is invalid.

⇒ Conclusively, only statements (a) and (c) correctly describe the properties of a triangle.

∴ The correct answer is (a) and (c).

Additional Information

Triangle Inequality Theorem

For any triangle possessing sides a, b, and c, the theorem declares: a + b > c, a + c > b, and b + c > a. Furthermore, the difference between any two sides is always strictly less than the length of the third side.

Exterior Angle Property

The scalar measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is mathematically equivalent to the sum of the measures of its two opposing (remote) interior angles.

Classification of Triangles (by Angles)

Acute (all interior angles are strictly less than 90°), Right (possesses exactly one 90° angle), and Obtuse (possesses exactly one interior angle strictly greater than 90°).

questions.q: What is the total surface area of a cone whose curved surface area is 550 cm² and radius is 7 cm ? ( Take π = 22/7).
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The Total Surface Area (TSA) of a cone is directly the sum of its Curved Surface Area (CSA) and its Base Area.

Base Area = π × r² = (22/7) × 7 × 7 = 154 cm²

TSA = CSA + Base Area = 550 + 154 = 704 cm²

∴ The correct answer is 704.00 cm².

Alternate Method



Given:

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 550 cm²

Radius of the base (r) = 7 cm

Formula Used:

CSA of a cone = πrl (where l is the slant height)

Total Surface Area (TSA) = πr(l + r)

Calculations:

⇒ π × r × l = 550

⇒ (22/7) × 7 × l = 550

⇒ 22 × l = 550

⇒ l = 550 ÷ 22 = 25 cm

⇒ TSA = π × r × (l + r)

⇒ TSA = (22/7) × 7 × (25 + 7)

⇒ TSA = 22 × 32

⇒ TSA = 704 cm²

∴ The correct answer is 704.00 cm².

Additional Information

Volume of a Cone

The volume of a cone is one-third the volume of a cylinder with the same base radius and height. Formula: V = (1/3)πr²h

Slant Height Relationship

The slant height (l), radius (r), and perpendicular height (h) form a right-angled triangle. By Pythagoras theorem: l² = r² + h²

Surface Area Comparison

Curved Surface Area is just the lateral conical covering (πrl). Total Surface Area includes both this lateral cover and the flat circular bottom base (πr²).

∴ The correct answer is 22.22%.

Alternate Method



Given:

Two successive percentage increases of 25%.

Two successive percentage decreases of 25%.

Formula Used:

Effective % change = A + B + (A × B) ÷ 100

Percentage less = [(Greater Value − Smaller Value) ÷ Greater Value] × 100

Calculation:

⇒ For two successive decreases of 25%:

⇒ Effective decrease = 25 + 25 − (25 × 25) ÷ 100

⇒ Effective decrease = 50 − 6.25 = 43.75%

⇒ For two successive increases of 25%:

⇒ Effective increase = 25 + 25 + (25 × 25) ÷ 100

⇒ Effective increase = 50 + 6.25 = 56.25%

⇒ Difference between the two values = 56.25% − 43.75% = 12.5%

⇒ Percentage by which decrease is less than increase = (Difference ÷ Effective increase) × 100

⇒ Required % = (12.5 ÷ 56.25) × 100

⇒ Required % = (1250 ÷ 5625) × 100

⇒ Required % = (2 ÷ 9) × 100 = 200 ÷ 9 %

⇒ Required % ≈ 22.22%

∴ The correct answer is 22.22%.

Additional Information

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is subjected to two successive changes of x% and y%, the net change is given by (x + y + xy ÷ 100)%. Use a positive sign for an increase and a negative sign for a decrease.

Percentage Less / More

To find by what percent A is less than B, always take the difference with respect to the base value B using the formula: [(B − A) ÷ B] × 100.

Successive Discounts

For two successive discounts of d₁% and d₂%, the single equivalent discount formula directly evaluates as (d₁ + d₂ − d₁ × d₂ ÷ 100)%.

questions.q: If (48° + k) is an acute angle and sin(48° + k) = cos13°, what is the value of k(in °)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

If sin A = cos B for acute angles A and B, then A + B = 90°.

Here, A = 48° + k and B = 13°.

⇒ 48° + k + 13° = 90°

⇒ 61° + k = 90°

⇒ k = 29°

∴ The correct answer is 29°.

Alternate Method

Given:

sin(48° + k) = cos13°

Formula Used:

cos θ = sin(90° − θ)

Calculation:

⇒ sin(48° + k) = cos13°

⇒ sin(48° + k) = sin(90° − 13°)

⇒ sin(48° + k) = sin77°

Comparing the angles on both sides (since both are acute angles):

⇒ 48° + k = 77°

⇒ k = 77° − 48°

⇒ k = 29°

∴ The correct answer is 29°.

Additional Information

Complementary Angles

Two angles are complementary if their sum is 90°. Trigonometric ratios of complementary angles follow the rule: sin(90° − θ) = cos θ, tan(90° − θ) = cot θ, and sec(90° − θ) = cosec θ.

Supplementary Angles

Two angles are supplementary if their sum is 180°. For supplementary angles: sin(180° − θ) = sin θ, but cos(180° − θ) = −cos θ.

Basic Trigonometric Identities

The three fundamental identities in trigonometry are: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

sinθ = 1 / cosecθ, cosθ = 1 / secθ, and tanθ = 1 / cotθ.

For expressions independent of θ, substituting standard angles like 0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, or 90° directly yields the answer, provided no term becomes undefined.

questions.q: In a room, there are some chairs and some people. If on each chair, only one person is seated, then there is no chair for exactly one person. If on each chair, two persons sit, then there is one vacant chair. What is the number of chairs in the room?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let the number of chairs be C.

If 1 person sits per chair, 1 person is left over → Total People = C + 1.

If 2 persons sit per chair, 1 chair is vacant → Total People = 2 × (C − 1).

Equating both: C + 1 = 2C − 2 ⇒ C = 3.

∴ The correct answer is 3 chairs.

Alternate Method

Given:

⇒ Case 1: If 1 person sits on each chair, exactly 1 person has no chair.

⇒ Case 2: If 2 persons sit on each chair, exactly 1 chair is vacant.

Formula Used:

questions.q: A person first increases the price of a commodity by 8% and then he announces a discount of 18%. The actual discount (in%) on the original price is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Apply the successive percentage change formula: Net Change = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100

Here, a = +8 (increase) and b = −18 (discount).

Net Change = 8 − 18 + (8 × −18) ÷ 100

Net Change = −10 − 1.44 = −11.44%

The negative sign indicates an actual discount of 11.44% on the original price.

∴ The correct answer is 11.44%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial price markup = +8%

Discount announced = 18%



Calculations:

Let the original price of the commodity be 100.

⇒ Marked Price after 8% increase = 100 + 8% of 100

⇒ Marked Price = 100 + 8 = 108

⇒ Final Selling Price after 18% discount = Marked Price − 18% of Marked Price

⇒ Final Selling Price = 108 − (18 ÷ 100) × 108

⇒ Final Selling Price = 108 − 19.44 = 88.56

⇒ Total discount amount = Original Price − Final Selling Price

⇒ Total discount amount = 100 − 88.56 = 11.44

⇒ Since the assumed original price is 100, the overall discount percentage is strictly equal to the discount amount.

∴ The correct answer is 11.44%.

Additional Information

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is sequentially changed by a% and then by b%, the effective overall percentage change is a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100. Always use a positive sign for an increase and a negative sign for a decrease or discount.

Discount vs Markup

Markup is always calculated on the Cost Price to arrive at the Marked Price (MP). A discount is invariably provided on the Marked Price to arrive at the Final Selling Price.

Effective Discount of Two Successive Discounts

For two sequential discounts of x% and y%, the net single equivalent discount magnitude is given directly by x + y − (x × y) ÷ 100.

questions.q: Two athletes are participating in a race on a circular track of 220 m. Ravi runs at the speed of 22 m/s, while Kapil runs at the speed of 11 m/s. They start from the same point, at the same time and in the same direction. After how many seconds will they meet for the first time?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When running in the same direction on a circular track, the relative speed is the difference of their speeds.

Relative Speed = 22 − 11 = 11 m/s

Time to meet = Track Length ÷ Relative Speed

Time = 220 ÷ 11 = 20 seconds

∴ The correct answer is 20 seconds.

Alternate Method

Given:

Length of the circular track = 220 m

Speed of Ravi = 22 m/s

Speed of Kapil = 11 m/s



Formula Used:

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Relative speed (same direction) = Speed 1 − Speed 2

Calculations:

⇒ Relative speed = 22 − 11 = 11 m/s

⇒ Time taken to meet = Total distance ÷ Relative speed

⇒ Time taken = 220 ÷ 11

⇒ Time taken = 20 seconds

∴ The correct answer is 20 seconds.

Additional Information

Meeting at the Starting Point

The time taken to meet exactly at the starting point for the first time is the LCM of the individual times taken by each runner to complete one full round.

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two bodies move in opposite directions around a track, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Number of Distinct Meeting Points

When running in the same direction, the total number of distinct meeting points on the circular track is the difference of their speeds when expressed in their simplest ratio.

questions.q: If books bought at prices ranging from ₹200 to ₹260 are sold at prices ranging from ₹250 to 300, what is the greatest possible profit that might be made in selling 25 books?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

To obtain the greatest possible profit, the books must be bought at the lowest possible price and sold at the highest possible price.

Maximum Profit per book = Maximum Selling Price − Minimum Cost Price = 300 − 200 = ₹100.

Greatest profit for 25 books = 25 × 100 = ₹2500.

∴ The correct answer is ₹2500.

Alternate Method

Given:

Cost price of books ranges from ₹200 to ₹260.

Selling price of books ranges from ₹250 to ₹300.

Total number of books to be sold = 25.

Formula Used:

Profit = Selling Price (SP) − Cost Price (CP)



Calculation:

⇒ For maximum profit, the cost price must be the minimum possible and the selling price must be the maximum possible.

⇒ Minimum Cost Price (CP) of one book = ₹200

⇒ Maximum Selling Price (SP) of one book = ₹300

⇒ Maximum profit per book = Maximum SP − Minimum CP

⇒ Maximum profit per book = 300 − 200 = ₹100

⇒ Total greatest possible profit for 25 books = 25 × 100 = ₹2500

∴ The correct answer is ₹2500.

Additional Information

Maximum vs Minimum Profit

Maximum profit is obtained when the Cost Price is minimum and Selling Price is maximum. Conversely, minimum profit (or maximum loss) occurs when the Cost Price is maximum and Selling Price is minimum.

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100. Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100. Percentage is always calculated on the original Cost Price unless specified otherwise in the question.

Selling Price Formula

When Profit % is given: SP = CP × (100 + Profit %) ÷ 100. When Loss % is given: SP = CP × (100 − Loss %) ÷ 100.

questions.q: Three people, A, B and C, invest in a business in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5. It was decided that 9% of the profits will go to charity. If the total profit was ₹2,50,000, then find the share of C in the profit (in ₹).
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

C's share fraction = 5 ÷ (2 + 3 + 5) = 1/2 of the distributable profit.

Profit remaining after charity = 100% − 9% = 91% of total profit.

C's share = 1/2 × 91% of 2,50,000

C's share = (45.5 ÷ 100) × 2,50,000 = 1,13,750

∴ The correct answer is ₹1,13,750.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of investments of A, B and C = 2 : 3 : 5

Total profit = ₹2,50,000

Percentage of profit given to charity = 9%

Formula Used:

Distributable Profit = Total Profit × ((100 − Charity%) ÷ 100)

Profit Share = (Individual Ratio ÷ Total Ratio) × Distributable Profit



Calculations:

⇒ Distributable profit = 2,50,000 × ((100 − 9) ÷ 100)

⇒ Distributable profit = 2,50,000 × (91 ÷ 100) = ₹2,27,500

⇒ Total ratio parts = 2 + 3 + 5 = 10 parts

⇒ C's profit share ratio = 5 parts

⇒ Share of C = (5 ÷ 10) × 2,27,500

⇒ Share of C = 1/2 × 2,27,500 = 1,13,750

∴ The correct answer is ₹1,13,750.

Additional Information

Simple Partnership

When all partners invest their capitals for the same time period, the profit is distributed exactly in the ratio of their invested capitals.

Compound Partnership

When partners invest for different time periods, the profit ratio is calculated dynamically as (Capital₁ × Time₁) : (Capital₂ × Time₂).

Active vs Sleeping Partner

An active partner gets a separate fixed share or salary for managing the business operations, and the remaining profit is then divided among all partners based on their capital investments.

Weighted Average

Alligation Rule

questions.q: If (3(16³ - 6³))/(16² + 6² + Q) = 30, then find the value of Q.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The expression follows the identity: a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²).

Substitute a = 16 and b = 6, yielding a − b = 10 and ab = 16 × 6 = 96.

The numerator becomes 3 × 10 × (16² + 6² + 96) = 30(16² + 6² + 96).

Given the RHS is 30, the denominator (16² + 6² + Q) must be equal to (16² + 6² + 96).

By direct comparison, Q = 96.

∴ The correct answer is 96.

Alternate Method

Given:

[3(16³ − 6³)] ÷ (16² + 6² + Q) = 30

Formula Used:

a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + b² + ab)

Calculations:

⇒ 16³ − 6³ = (16 − 6)(16² + 6² + 16 × 6)

⇒ 16³ − 6³ = 10(16² + 6² + 96)

⇒ [3 × 10(16² + 6² + 96)] ÷ (16² + 6² + Q) = 30

⇒ 30(16² + 6² + 96) ÷ (16² + 6² + Q) = 30

⇒ 16² + 6² + 96 = 16² + 6² + Q

⇒ Q = 96

∴ The correct answer is 96.

Additional Information

Sum of Cubes Identity

a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²). The middle term of the trinomial factor is always negative.

Difference of Squares

a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b). This is highly useful for simplifying numerators and denominators.

Algebraic Expansions

(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² and (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b².

questions.q: ΔABC is a right-angled triangle with ∠ABC = 90°. If m(AB) = 28 cm, and m(BC) = 96 cm, find the area (in cm²) of the circumcircle of ΔABC. (Use π = 3.14.)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For a right-angled triangle, the circumcenter always lies at the midpoint of the hypotenuse.

This means the hypotenuse acts as the diameter of the circumcircle.

Using the standard Pythagorean triplet (7, 24, 25), we multiply by 4 to get sides (28, 96, 100), making hypotenuse AC = 100 cm.

Circumradius (R) = 100 ÷ 2 = 50 cm.

Area of circumcircle = π × R² = 3.14 × 2500 = 7850 cm².

∴ The correct answer is 7850 cm².

Alternate Method

Given:

m(AB) = 28 cm

m(BC) = 96 cm

∠ABC = 90°

π = 3.14



Formula Used:

Hypotenuse = √(Perpendicular² + Base²)

Circumradius (R) = Hypotenuse ÷ 2

Area of Circle = π × R²

Calculations:

⇒ In right-angled ΔABC, apply Pythagorean theorem to find hypotenuse AC:

⇒ AC = √(AB² + BC²)

⇒ AC = √(28² + 96²)

⇒ AC = √(784 + 9216)

⇒ AC = √10000 = 100 cm

⇒ The hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle forms the diameter of its circumcircle.

⇒ Circumradius (R) = AC ÷ 2

⇒ Circumradius (R) = 100 ÷ 2 = 50 cm

⇒ Area of Circumcircle = 3.14 × (50)²

⇒ Area = 3.14 × 2500

⇒ Area = 7850 cm²

∴ The correct answer is 7850 cm².

Additional Information

Circumcenter of a Right-Angled Triangle

The circumcenter lies exactly at the midpoint of the hypotenuse, making the circumradius equal to half the hypotenuse (R = h ÷ 2).

Inradius of a Right-Angled Triangle

The radius of the inscribed circle can be calculated directly using the formula r = (Perpendicular + Base − Hypotenuse) ÷ 2.

Pythagorean Triplets

A set of three positive integers (a, b, c) that satisfy a² + b² = c². Common primitive triplets include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (7, 24, 25).

questions.q: If ₹1,875 becomes ₹2,625 in 4 years, what will ₹24,000 become at the end of 9 years at the same rate of interest, under simple interest?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Interest for 4 years = 2625 − 1875 = ₹750

Rate % = (750 × 100) ÷ (1875 × 4) = 10%

Interest on ₹24000 for 9 years at 10% = (24000 × 10 × 9) ÷ 100 = ₹21600

Total Amount = Principal + Interest = 24000 + 21600 = ₹45600

∴ The correct answer is ₹45600.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal P₁ = ₹1875, Amount A₁ = ₹2625, Time T₁ = 4 years

Principal P₂ = ₹24000, Time T₂ = 9 years

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount = P + SI



Calculations:

⇒ SI₁ = A₁ − P₁ = 2625 − 1875 = ₹750

⇒ R = (SI₁ × 100) ÷ (P₁ × T₁)

⇒ R = (750 × 100) ÷ (1875 × 4) = 75000 ÷ 7500 = 10%

⇒ SI₂ = (P₂ × R × T₂) ÷ 100

⇒ SI₂ = (24000 × 10 × 9) ÷ 100 = ₹21600

⇒ A₂ = P₂ + SI₂

⇒ A₂ = 24000 + 21600 = ₹45600

∴ The correct answer is ₹45600.

Additional Information

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In Simple Interest, the principal remains constant throughout the entire period, whereas in Compound Interest, the principal periodically increases as the generated interest is added to it.

Direct Proportion in Simple Interest

For a fixed principal amount and rate of interest, the total Simple Interest earned is directly proportional to the elapsed time period.

questions.q: If A is an acute angle and tanA + cotA = 2, find the value of 7tan⁸A - 6cot⁸A + 8sec²A.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given tanA + cotA = 2. Since cotA = 1 ÷ tanA, the equation is in the form x + 1/x = 2, which always means x = 1.

Therefore, tanA = 1 and cotA = 1, which implies the angle A = 45°.

For A = 45°, secA = √2.

Substitute these directly into 7tan⁸A − 6cot⁸A + 8sec²A:

⇒ 7(1)⁸ − 6(1)⁸ + 8(√2)² = 7 − 6 + 16 = 17

∴ The correct answer is 17.

Alternate Method

Given:

tanA + cotA = 2 (where A is an acute angle)

Formula Used:

cotA = 1 ÷ tanA

sec²A = 1 + tan²A



Calculations:

⇒ tanA + 1/tanA = 2

⇒ (tan²A + 1) ÷ tanA = 2

⇒ tan²A − 2tanA + 1 = 0

⇒ (tanA − 1)² = 0

⇒ tanA = 1

⇒ Since A is an acute angle, A = 45°

⇒ cotA = 1 and secA = √2

Now, evaluate the given expression: 7tan⁸A − 6cot⁸A + 8sec²A

⇒ 7(1)⁸ − 6(1)⁸ + 8(√2)²

⇒ 7(1) − 6(1) + 8(2)

⇒ 7 − 6 + 16

⇒ 1 + 16 = 17

∴ The correct answer is 17.

Additional Information

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental reciprocal and Pythagorean identities include cotθ = 1 ÷ tanθ and sec²θ − tan²θ = 1.

Algebraic Special Case

If any positive real number and its reciprocal sum to exactly 2 (x + 1/x = 2), then the number itself must be strictly equal to 1 (x = 1).

Trigonometric Values at 45°

For an acute angle of 45° (or π ÷ 4 radians), the values are tan(45°) = 1, cot(45°) = 1, and sec(45°) = √2.

questions.q: Find the remainder when 9²⁰ + 2 is divided by 4.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

By the remainder theorem, when 9 is divided by 4, the remainder is 1.

Therefore, the remainder of 9²⁰ divided by 4 is strictly 1²⁰ = 1.

Adding the constant 2, the overall remainder becomes 1 + 2 = 3.

∴ The correct answer is 3.

Alternate Method

Given:

Expression: (9²⁰ + 2) ÷ 4

Formula Used:

The remainder of (ax + r)ⁿ ÷ a is equal to rⁿ

Calculation:

⇒ 9 can be expressed in terms of the divisor 4 as (4 × 2) + 1

⇒ Substitute this into the given expression: ((4 × 2 + 1)²⁰ + 2) ÷ 4

⇒ Applying the binomial remainder formula, the remainder of (4 × 2 + 1)²⁰ ÷ 4 reduces to 1²⁰

⇒ 1²⁰ = 1

⇒ Total remainder = Remainder of 9²⁰ + Remainder of 2

⇒ Total remainder = 1 + 2

⇒ Total remainder = 3

Since 3 is less than the divisor 4, the final remainder remains 3.

∴ The correct answer is 3.

Additional Information

Modular Arithmetic Addition

The remainder of a sum is the sum of the individual remainders: (A + B) mod N = [(A mod N) + (B mod N)] mod N.

Binomial Remainder Theorem

For any expression (ax + r)ⁿ divided by 'a', every term in the expansion except the last contains 'a' and is fully divisible. The remainder depends solely on rⁿ.

Negative Remainder Strategy

If solving an expression like 3²⁰ ÷ 4, writing 3 as (4 − 1) gives a remainder of (−1)²⁰ = 1. This significantly speeds up calculations for bases close to the divisor.

Length of tangent AB = √(17² − 8²) = √(289 − 64) = √225 = 15 cm.

The quadrilateral ABCD consists of two congruent right-angled triangles (ΔABC and ΔADC).

Total Area = 2 × Area of ΔABC = 2 × (1/2 × Base × Height).
